name: The Spire Report
subcategory: elite financial and social news network
creator: Vantage Media Collective (Tier 5 private consortium)
description: An invitation-only neural feed network accessible exclusively through Tier 5 BCI authentication, The Spire Report delivers financial intelligence, political forecasting, and social scheduling content to Meridian's ultra-elite with a frankness that licensed public networks cannot match — because it never pretends to be anything other than a service for people who own the other networks. Its content includes candid corponation acquisition intelligence, Spire social event coordination, and occasional long-form analysis pieces that acknowledge, with clinical detachment, the structural conditions producing the Gray Zone poverty. It does not editorialize about those conditions.
medium: neural feed (Tier 5 BCI authentication required), encrypted haptic briefings
cultural_impact: The Spire Report's existence is technically public knowledge but its content is entirely inaccessible below Tier 4 authentication; its occasional leaks — always partial, always curated — fuel intense speculation about what the city's owners actually know and say to each other.
controversy: A 2220 partial leak published by Okafor-Steinberg revealed a Spire Report analysis from 2218 that accurately predicted the Sable Charter labor action three months before it occurred and outlined optimal corponation response strategies — suggesting the Report functions as a coordination mechanism between ostensibly competing corponations.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 data courier is hired to physically transport a Spire Report authentication token — the kind of job that doesn't officially exist — and begins to realize what they're actually carrying and why someone wants to intercept it.

A Tier 5 subscriber to The Spire Report wants to leak a specific edition to an underground journalist but cannot do so without compromising their own authentication signature; they need an intermediary with very specific technical skills.
The Spire Report has gone dark for 72 hours — its authentication servers are not responding — and the silence in Tier 5 circles is louder than any broadcast.
